On The 1 st Of April, 2026
 Criminal Appeal No. 3888 of 2021
 Awadhesh Kumar Saket
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Sankalp Kochar, learned counsel for the appellant.
 Shri Ajay Shukla, learned Public Prosecutor for the respon
 Judgment
(Dictated In Open Court) Per: Justice Vivek Agarwal
Learned counsel for the appellant prays for withdrawal of I.A. No.2359/2026, which is the first application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
Accordingly, I.A. No.2359/2026 is dismissed as withdrawn.
With the consent of learned counsel for the parties, the case is heard finally.

This criminal appeal under Section 374(2) of the Cr.P.C. is filed by the appellant being aggrieved of the judgment dated 27/02/2020 passed by the learned Special Judge, POCSO Act/23rd Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal (MP) in Sessions Trial No.588/2019 whereby the learned trial Court has convicted and sentenced the appellant as under :

It is submitted that as per medical evidence given by Dr.Pranati Kumar (PW-5), there was no sign of any external or internal injuries on the body of the victim.

This witness examined vulva, labia,
majora, minora anus, thighs and nearabout areas of the victim and had not found any injury.
Hymen of the victim was intact and vaginal swab was drawn.
No human semen was found on Articles 'A', 'B', 'C', 'D1', 'D/2', 'D/3' i.e. the slide, swab, rectal swab and clothings of the victim.

Thus,
it is submitted that it will be a case under Section 7 of POCSO Act i.e. of sexual assault.
This sexual assault was committed on a girl less than 12 years of age, therefore, offence will be covered under Section 9(m) of the POCSO Act punishable under Section 10 of POCSO Act.

Reliance is place on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Laxman Jangde Vs. State of Chhattisgarh through the Station House Officer, in Criminal Appeal No..../2025 (Arising out of SLP (Crl.) No.10377 of 2025) where under the similar facts and circumstances, Hon'ble Supreme Court has altered the conviction from one under Section 376 AB of the IPC to one under Section 10 of POCSO Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:25680 3 CRA-3888-2021 3.
Shri Ajay Shukla, learned Public Prosecutor for the State, opposes the prayer and submits that victim (PW-2) has given a vivid description of the act.
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
On going through the evidence of the victim (PW-2) and also the evidence of lady doctor i.e. Dr. Pranati Kumar (PW-5), it is a case of sexual assault as defined under Section 7 of the POCSO Act.

Since the victim was less than 12 years of age, it will be covered under Section 9(m) of the POCSO Act and not under Section 6 of the POCSO Act as there is no element of any penetrative sexual assault normal or aggravated as defined under Section 3/5 of the POCSO Act, therefore, we are of the opinion that in view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Laxman Jangde (supra) , where the facts were almost similar,
conviction of the appellant can be altered from one under Section 376 AB to Section 9(m) of the POCSO Act.
Thus, the conviction of the appellant under Section 376 AB of IPC is hereby altered to Section 9(m) of POCSO Act.

Hence, impugned judgment dated 27/02/2020 passed by the learned Special Judge, POCSO Act/23rd Additional Sessions Judge, Bhopal (MP) in Sessions Trial No.588/2019 is modified to the extent that instead of Section 376AB of the IPC, the appellant is convicted under Section 9(m) of POCSO Act and he is directed to undergo R.I. for seven years along with fine of Rs.2,000/- with a default stipulation to undergo additional S.I. for one month.
